taxonomy.wholeLinuxVmWorkloadSupport: Target-native reconstruction of a declared Linux VM workload context from retained portable artifacts and verifiers.

supportedSubsetCandidate.description: A tiny declared VM workload whose rootfs/app files, workload command, input data, expected outputs, and target verifier are all represented by portable retained artifacts.

requiredSupportedRows.requirement: Target VM boots target-native Linux without source kernel/CPU replay.
Rootfs/app files are reconstructed from portable artifacts with hashes.
Workload command restarts/reconstructs from declared state, not raw process memory.
Source and target verifier outputs prove equivalent workload behavior.
Both arm64-to-amd64 and amd64-to-arm64 directions retain capture, restore, transcript, manifest, and verifier artifacts.

refusalBoundaries.reason: Source vCPU/register state cannot be replayed across ISA boundaries.
Opaque guest kernel/device state is not a portable workload artifact.
Arbitrary process memory/register continuation remains separate and currently 0.
Active connections require protocol-aware reconstruction or reconnect policy.
Live mount/FUSE state must be represented by explicit portable mount artifacts or refused.
Dirty block-device state without a portable manifest cannot be treated as restored.
Source-architecture kernel modules or ABI-specific dependencies are not portable across target architectures.
eBPF, seccomp, KVM/nested virtualization, and similar features need retained capability probes and explicit refusal rows.

forbiddenShortcuts: app checkpoint hooks as the source of truth

dashboardClaimLanguage.notStarted: Whole Linux VM workload portability is definition-only. Current claim remains 0 / 0 / 0.
dashboardClaimLanguage.futureIfProven: Selected whole-VM workload restore: 100 / 100 / 0 for selected-whole-vm-workload-v1 only.
dashboardClaimLanguage.requiredBoundaryText: Not arbitrary VM restore, not raw cross-ISA VM-state replay, and not arbitrary Linux process restore.
